_comment: Named address ranges of The Simpsons Game (USA, default.xex) image for the inventory. kind: library = statically linked SDK code, replaced as a unit by Any360 (not decompiled); middleware = third-party engine code the title links (physics, AI, vegetation, scripting, video): neither the title's own code nor something Any360 provides, so it stays recompiled or is replaced by the vendor's library for the target, never decompiled function by function; game = the title's own code. Evidence (tools/library_scan.py), three kinds read together: functions with the same sequence of instruction mnemonics (14 instructions or more) as a function of another title, clustered; the strings a range refers to (lis/addi pairs into the decrypted image); the system calls it makes. Each range runs from its first to its last function carrying such evidence, so it may be a little short, not long. What names each: the D3D runtime shares its functions with Crackdown's and Test Drive Unlimited's (the port's re/d3d_method_table.md places its command writers at 0x82461500, inside it); D3DX and XGraphics share theirs with Crackdown's (the HLSL compiler, 'D3DXValidIndices', the X file loader's 'xof 0303txt' templates, the image loaders); Havok by its strings ('** Havok libs built with version [', '.\collide\mopp\machine\...', 'hkClassEnumItem') and the functions it shares with the other two titles' Havok (fewer: another build, with thread-local memory); Lua by the messages of Lua 5.0 and Crackdown's Lua; the CRT by 'Visual C++ CRT: Not enough memory', KeTls* / KeBugCheck and the port's crt_native.cpp bindings (0x82A3Cxxx); XDK audio, Xbox Live and XAPI by the functions they share with the other two titles and their system calls. The import thunks are the addresses generated simpsons_init.cpp binds. Not named for want of evidence: 0x82B8D518-0x82BBD388 (between two parts of D3DX), 0x82A65F38-0x82A8B5A0 (a path rasterizer: 'curveto %f %f ...'). Ranges outside the list are reported by 1 MB area until symbol recovery names them.
